summary.text: One of the fifty daughters of Danaus by Crino — by lot the bride of Hyperbius son of Egyptus when the sons of Aegyptus married the Danaids at Argos; distinct from Celaeno the Pleiad and from Celaeno the Harpy.

story.text: Apollodorus lists Celaeno third among the daughters of Danaus borne on Crino. When the youngest sons of Egyptus by Hephaestine cast lots, Hyperbius drew Celaeno. On the wedding night she received her father's dagger and, like her sisters, slew her bridegroom — Hyginus names the man she killed as Aristonoos rather than Hyperbius.
